name: Essence step

card.summary: The lightweight, watery layer in Korean-style skincare routines, applied after cleansing and toning to add hydration and prepare skin for serums and moisturizer.

quick.overview:
The essence step is one stage of the multi-step Korean skincare routine. An essence is a thin, watery product applied after cleansing and before heavier serums, creams and sunscreen. It is meant to hydrate and support the products that follow.

Its payoff is skin that looks more hydrated and smooth, which people associate with a clearer, healthier complexion. The step belongs to the broader K-beauty trend, where routines of around ten steps became popular in the 2010s.
quick.how: After cleansing, essence is pressed or patted onto skin, usually morning and night, before serum, moisturizer and, in the day, sunscreen. Ingredients vary by product, with hydrating humectants and fermented or botanical extracts commonly marketed.
quick.risks: Irritation or allergy to a particular ingredient or fragrance is possible, as with any topical product. Patch testing and consulting a dermatologist are the usual guidance for sensitive or reactive skin.

lead: The essence step is a stage in Korean skincare routines in which a lightweight, water-based product called an essence is applied between toner and serum. K-beauty routines typically include cleansing (often a double cleanse), sheet masks, essences, serums, moisturizers and sunscreen, and have been described as averaging about ten steps [1].

People use essence to boost hydration and prepare skin for later products, aiming for a smoother, more even-looking complexion. K-beauty reached Western markets prominently with BB creams in 2011, and Korean pop culture and tourism helped spread routines [1].

chain: Apply a light hydrating essence after cleansing
Serums and moisturizer layer on top for a smoother look
angle.text: The essence adds a layer of hydration that people describe as improving skin texture and glow when used alongside the rest of a routine.

paras: In the K-beauty sequence, essence follows cleansing and precedes serum and moisturizer; at night a sleep cream may replace sunscreen [1].
Market data cited by Wikipedia says that South Korea accounted for a large share of global skincare launches, and a drama sponsorship by Amorepacific reportedly lifted skincare sales [1].

timeline.event: BB cream reaches Western markets, often cited as the start of K-beauty's spread [1].
